@brandonhare Thank you for reporting the crash and your detailed investigation!

I've applied a fix based on your findings, but with a more fundamental approach instead of the workaround in your PR.

**The issue:**
`IMF2DBuffer::Lock2D` returns `ppbScanline0` pointing to the last row and a negative `pitch` for bottom-up (flipped)
images.

**Your proposed fix (workaround):**
Detect flipped images and manually adjust the pointer back to the buffer start.

**Applied fix (fundamental approach):**
Use the `pitch` value directly as Microsoft recommends: `scan_line0 + y * pitch`. When pitch is negative, this naturally
iterates backward through the buffer, eliminating the need for manual flip detection.

Additionally, I found that the `buffer->Lock()` fallback path also requires bottom-up handling when using Media Foundation
conversion (RGB format).

@siliconspecter 
I read through your code — the issues are in how the feed is displayed:

- A Sprite2D sizes itself from the CameraTexture, which always reports the Y-plane (full) resolution, so the half-width CbCr plane gets distorted. Combine the planes in a ShaderMaterial instead (the demo uses a TextureRect + shader).
- RGB and YCbCr feeds need different CameraTexture.which_feed values — use FEED_RGBA_IMAGE for RGB, and FEED_Y_IMAGE + FEED_CBCR_IMAGE for separate YCbCr. Pick them based on get_datatype().
- Please try the demo project to see it working: https://github.com/shiena/godot-camerafeed-demo/

As for the RGB32 crash, that looks like a separate issue — could you share the output from running with --verbose? That would help me track it down.

Out of curiosity, on [the branch which is taken in the sample](https://github.com/shiena/godot-camerafeed-demo/blob/fa6b1681958705668ed2aea4142c54d562ef44b0/ycbcr_to_rgb.gdshader#L44), it seems to use the same texture co-ordinate for both Y and CbCr.  I guess this means that Sprite2D is doing something to the UVs its end?  I wouldn't have expected that.

Right — it's not Sprite2D touching the UVs. In the shader, UV is normalized [0, 1], and each sampler2D maps that range onto its own texture size. So the same UV hits the matching spot in the full-res Y plane and the half-width CbCr
plane, and the GPU resamples the chroma for you — that's why one UV works for both.

YCbCr keeps luma (Y) at full resolution and chroma (CbCr) subsampled (for YUY2, half width), so you reconstruct the image by sampling both planes with normalized UVs and converting to RGB in the shader.

What broke earlier wasn't the sprite editing UVs: when you bind the CameraTexture directly, the sprite is sized from CameraTexture.get_width(), which always reports the Y/base (full) resolution even for the CbCr plane. So it drew a
full-width quad over a half-width texture and the UVs ran past 1.0 (edge-clamped) — a size-reporting quirk of CameraTexture, not Sprite2D.

@siliconspecter 
I've pushed a fix for the RGB32 crash — could you grab a fresh build and try again?

The decoder was uploading frames to the RenderingServer directly from the capture thread, which isn't allowed (creating/updating textures has to happen on the main thread). It now hands each frame off via call_deferred, matching what
the Android backend already does. Your RGB 1080p60 feed just has a high enough data rate to hit the race every time.
